newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Commission verifies Belgrade assembly mandates.
newsitem.headline: Commission verifies Belgrade assembly mandates.

text.p: The Belgrade city election commission removed on Thursday the last legal obstacle to the opposition assuming control of the city assembly by verifying the mandates of newly elected deputies after months of delay.

The move follows last week's capitulation by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to 12 weeks of protests over election fraud which deprived Zajedno of its victory in Belgrade and Serbia's 13 other biggest cities.
"The Belgrade municipal electoral commission verified today all the 110 council seats," commission president Radomir Lazarevic told a news conference.

"The city electoral commission has also informed Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic that it has completed its work and now there is a legal deadline of five days for Tomic to convene the city council constituent session," Lazarevic said.
According to these results, the opposition Zajedno coalition won 67 seats, the ruling leftist coalition 24, the radical party 17 and the democratic party of Serbia two.

The Serbian parliament passed a special law on Tuesday reinstating Zajedno gains in the November 17 elections initially erased by legal manoeuverings by the ruling socialists which also caused an outcry in the west.
